nl_info.title: AXT, Inc. Announces Q2 Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results
nl_info.sub_title: Revenue reached $47.6 million, beating expectations, with indium phosphide revenue hitting a record $30.7 million and plans to double capacity in 2026; shares surged over 36% premarket

summary.value: AXT, Inc. (AXTI) reported revenue of $47.6 million for Q2 FY2026, exceeding the market consensus of $34.08 million, more than doubling from Q1 and surging 165% YoY. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.19, significantly beating the analyst consensus of $0.07. GAAP net income turned profitable at $11.1 million, with EBIT at $10.42 million. Driven by strong results and AI optical communication demand, AXT's shares surged over 36% premarket. CEO Morris Young stated the business has reached a turning point, attributing growth to data center optical interconnect demand, with indium phosphide revenue reaching a record $30.7 million. Additionally, the company provided Q3 Non-GAAP EPS guidance of $0.30-$0.32, announced that its subsidiary Beijing Tongmei will shift its IPO plan from the STAR Market to Hong Kong, and revealed plans to double indium phosphide capacity in 2026.

invest_anal.value: The company reported a substantial sequential increase in revenue, which rose from $26.9 million in Q1 to $47.6 million in Q2, representing a quarter-over-quarter growth of approximately 77%. This expansion was driven by record revenue in the indium phosphide segment and increased demand within the data center optical interconnect market. Additionally, GAAP net income reached $11.1 million, compared to the previous period's performance.

eli_explain.value: AXT, Inc. (AXTI) reported its Q2 fiscal year 2026 financial results, featuring revenue of $47.6 million, which more than doubled from $26.9 million in Q1 and exceeded the consensus estimate of $34.1 million. [citation 1][citation 2] The company swung to a GAAP net income of $11.1 million, or $0.17 per diluted share, from a net loss in the previous quarter. [citation 2] Adjusted net income reached $11.9 million, surpassing the estimated $4.41 million. [citation 1][citation 3] GAAP gross margin expanded significantly to 44.9% from 29.6% in Q1. [citation 2] The performance was driven by record revenue in indium phosphide and strong demand for data center optical connectivity. [citation 1][citation 2]

A specialized high-tech kitchen recently saw its quarterly sales jump from $26.9 million to $47.6 million as a particular high-demand ingredient, indium phosphide, reached record-breaking popularity. By increasing its cooking capacity and improving kitchen efficiency, the establishment transformed a previous operating loss into a clear profit of $11.1 million.

The kitchen's efficiency also improved markedly, with the portion of each sale kept after covering ingredient costs rising from 29.6% to 44.9%. This shift occurred as the restaurant focused on serving the surging needs of large-scale data processing centers, which required their specialized high-performance products to function.

Quality: AXT demonstrated a significant recovery in profitability, swinging from a Q1 loss to a GAAP net income of $11.1 million. [citation 2] The GAAP gross margin expanded by 15.3 percentage points to 44.9%, reflecting improved manufacturing capacity and productivity. [citation 1][citation 2] Growth: Revenue grew by approximately 77% sequentially, driven by record quarterly indium phosphide revenue and demand for data center optical connectivity. [citation 1][citation 2] The company also recently signed a long-term supplier agreement with Lumentum involving a future $43.5 million deposit. [citation 4][citation 5] Momentum: Following the announcement of the Lumentum agreement and ahead of the full earnings release, the stock surged 22.92% in a single day. [citation 6] Prior to the release, the median 12-month price target was reported at $93.00, and the stock traded at a forward P/E ratio of 64 times earnings, compared to 1,232 three months prior. [citation 1]

AXT, Inc. delivered Q2 2026 results that exceeded analyst expectations for both revenue and adjusted net income, supported by record indium phosphide sales and a sharp expansion in gross margins. While the company has not provided specific future financial guidance, the recent performance highlights a shift to profitability and increased demand within the data center optical connectivity market. [citation 1][citation 2]

nl_info.title: AXT and Lumentum Sign Indium Phosphide Wafer Supply and Capacity Reservation Agreement Through 2031
nl_info.sub_title: Lumentum to pay $87 million in prepayments to secure InP wafer supply through 2031

summary.value: AXT, Inc. (AXTI.US) and Lumentum Holdings Inc. (LITE.US) have entered into a long-term supply and capacity reservation agreement for Indium Phosphide (InP) wafer substrates, effective through December 31, 2031. The agreement aims to address supply risks arising from the growing demand for AI data centers and high-speed optical modules. Under the terms, Lumentum will pay a total of $87 million in prepayments in two installments of $43.5 million each. The first installment will be paid within 30 working days of the agreement's effectiveness, while the second is expected in 2028 with specific conditions to be negotiated. These payments will serve as credits for future product purchases. Additionally, AXT has committed to reserving minimum annual supply capacity and supporting the customer's future expansion needs.

invest_anal.value: The long-term agreement provides AXT with revenue visibility and demand commitment through 2031 for its Indium Phosphide (InP) wafer substrates. The $87 million deposit functions as a credit against future purchases, representing a contractually secured baseline for future product volume. For Lumentum, the agreement secures the necessary capacity to support its own long-term production scaling requirements in the InP market.

- **Momentum**: Market activity reflects high demand for AI-related optical components; Lumentum shares increased by 312.2% over a recent six-month period, significantly outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 3.3% return. Analysts note that Lumentum's fiscal 2026 third-quarter earnings are estimated at $2.25 per share, representing a 294.74% year-over-year growth forecast. [citation 7][citation 3]

AXT and Lumentum have established a strategic supply partnership lasting through 2031, supported by $87 million in capacity reservation deposits from Lumentum. The agreement addresses a structural supply imbalance in the indium phosphide market, where AXT is expanding manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand from hyperscalers and AI infrastructure providers. # Indium Phosphide Wafer Market - Forecasts from 2025 to 2030. The indium phosphide wafer market, at a 11.02% CAGR, is expected to grow to USD 432.037 million in 2030 from USD 256.144 million in 2025. The indium phosphide (InP) wafer market serves as a critical foundation for advanced semiconductor applications that demand superior performance beyond the capabilities of silicon. The established infrastructure for 6-inch wafers allows for economies of scale, which is essential for making advanced LiDAR and 3D sensing systems commercially viable for mass-market applications. The availability of high-performance InP devices, such as multi-junction VCSEL arrays and edge-emitting lasers, on this larger wafer format signifies the market's maturation and its readiness to support high-volume manufacturing for a diverse set of advanced applications. nl_info.title: Beijing Tongmei Terminates STAR Market IPO Registration
nl_info.sub_title: The IPO process for the AXT, Inc. subsidiary concluded after over four years, having previously planned to raise 1.167 billion RMB.

summary.value: On the evening of July 8, the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) disclosed that Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology Co., Ltd. (Beijing Tongmei) has terminated its registration for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Sci-Tech Innovation Board (STAR Market). The termination resulted from the company's voluntary withdrawal of its listing application and related registration documents. Beijing Tongmei, which specializes in semiconductor substrate materials, is a controlling subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed AXT, Inc. (AXTI). The company had previously planned to raise 1.167 billion RMB through the IPO. After submitting its registration application in August 2022, the process lasted nearly four years without approval, ultimately being terminated on July 2, 2026. Its prospectus has not been updated since 2022, lacking recent financial data.

invest_anal.value: The termination of Beijing Tongmei's STAR Market IPO registration concludes a four-year effort to establish an independent market valuation for this subsidiary. As the China-based operations of Nasdaq-listed AXT, Inc. (AXTI), the subsidiary's valuation will not be decoupled from the parent company through a secondary listing at this time. This event maintains the current asset structure where the valuation of the subsidiary remains reflected through the parent company's consolidated market capitalization rather than a separate market-determined price on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

eli_explain.value: On July 8, 2026, the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) announced the termination of the registration process for Beijing Tongmei Crystal Technology Co., Ltd.’s (Beijing Tongmei) Initial Public Offering (IPO) on the Sci-Tech Innovation Board (STAR Market). Beijing Tongmei is the primary China-based subsidiary of AXT, Inc. (NASDAQ: AXTI). This decision concludes an application process that had been active for over four years. [citation 1]

A large international restaurant group, AXT, had spent over four years preparing to list its major regional kitchen branch as an independent local business. This branch is responsible for preparing specialized ingredients used in high-end global dishes. After a long period of regulatory review and preparation, the plan to take this specific kitchen branch public has been officially withdrawn.

While the independent listing of the kitchen branch is no longer moving forward, the parent group continues its core operations. For instance, the branch recently secured a significant three-year contract to supply specialized ingredients to another major food service provider, ensuring its kitchen remains active despite the change in its corporate listing plans.

The termination of the IPO registration represents a shift in the corporate structure and financing strategy for the subsidiary and its parent company.

- Quality (75): Beijing Tongmei remains a key operational subsidiary for AXT, Inc., recently demonstrating its industrial standing by securing a three-year wafer supply agreement with Coherent Corp. [citation 2]
- Growth (60): While the termination halts the immediate influx of capital specifically from the STAR Market, the company's growth trajectory is currently supported by long-term supply contracts in the semiconductor materials sector. [citation 2]
- Momentum (55): Historically, news regarding this subsidiary has influenced the parent company's stock; for example, AXT, Inc. shares previously rose 6.5% in premarket trading following the announcement of a major supply deal involving Beijing Tongmei. Market participants are now observing the impact of the IPO withdrawal on capital flow. [citation 2]

The more than four-year effort to list Beijing Tongmei on the STAR Market has ended following the official termination of its IPO registration by the SSE. Beijing Tongmei continues to operate as a subsidiary of AXT, Inc., maintaining its role in the global supply chain through existing multi-year commercial agreements. [citation 2][citation 1]

nl_info.sub_title: China's control of approximately 70% of global indium supply has led to strategic shifts in the AI optical communications sector

summary.value: China's implementation of export licensing for indium-related materials has introduced supply chain risks for high-speed AI optical communications, specifically affecting 800G and 1.6T transceiver production. Coherent reported delays in license approvals and is expanding its 150mm Indium Phosphide (InP) manufacturing capacity in Texas with support from the CHIPS Act. Meanwhile, Nvidia has entered into long-term supply agreements and provided $2 billion in funding to both Coherent and Lumentum to secure critical optical components.

invest_anal.value: China's export controls on indium phosphide (InP), a material where China holds approximately 70% of global production, directly impact the supply chain stability and operational risks of optical communication companies. AXT reported a reduction in Q1 revenue guidance due to licensing delays, reflecting an immediate impact on asset turnover and operational efficiency. Conversely, Coherent is mitigating supply chain concentration risk by expanding its 150mm InP manufacturing capacity in Texas, supported by the CHIPS Act. The $2 billion funding provided by Nvidia to both Coherent and Lumentum represents a strategic adjustment to secure long-term component availability, which affects the balance sheet through increased liquidity and long-term contractual obligations.

eli_explain.value: China's implementation of export licensing for indium phosphide (InP) and related materials has introduced significant supply chain volatility for the AI optical communications sector. AXT Inc. (AXTI) reported substantial headwinds, including a reduction in revenue guidance for late 2025 due to fewer export permits being issued by China's Ministry of Commerce than anticipated. [citation 1][citation 2] While AXT's subsidiary, Tongmei, began receiving some permits in early 2026 to resume shipments to select customers, the process remains subject to timing-volatile interruptions. [citation 2][citation 3] Concurrently, AXT announced the withdrawal of Tongmei’s IPO application from the Shanghai STAR Market, shifting its listing focus to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to highlight its strategy centered on InP substrates for AI data centers. [citation 4] In the midstream, companies like Coherent (COHR) have reported expanded operating margins and a 56% rise in adjusted net income driven by AI demand, despite broader supply chain shifts. [citation 5]

The event highlights critical shifts in the semiconductor value chain across three dimensions:

- **Quality**: AXT’s fundamentals have been impacted by geopolitical factors, with the company reporting a GAAP net loss of $21.3 million for fiscal year 2025 and a non-GAAP gross margin that fluctuated from negative 6.1% to 29.9% in Q1 2026 as permit flow improved. [citation 2][citation 6] Coherent, by contrast, demonstrated fundamental resilience through higher factory utilization and supply chain efficiencies, leading to significant gains in adjusted net income. [citation 5]
- **Growth**: Demand for InP remains tied to the AI infrastructure build-out, with AXT projecting scale-out orders to potentially double in 2026 and 2027 as data centers shift toward high-speed optical connectivity. [citation 7][citation 8] The company is also planning to double its manufacturing capacity by late 2027 to meet this structural demand. [citation 6]
- **Momentum**: Market sentiment has been highly reactive to regulatory news; AXT’s stock experienced a 20% single-session plunge in April 2026 due to valuation concerns and share dilution, but later surged 14.46% in July 2026 following analyst upgrades and improved product pricing. [citation 9][citation 10] Coherent has maintained strong long-term momentum with a one-year total shareholder return of 247.80%, reflecting its central role in the AI datacom business. [citation 5]

China's export controls on indium phosphide have forced semiconductor substrate suppliers and optical component manufacturers to navigate a landscape of licensing delays and strategic realignments. While AXT has transitioned its subsidiary's listing to Hong Kong and reported a recovery in permit approvals, the broader industry—including Coherent—continues to balance surging AI-driven demand against the risks of concentrated material supply chains and geopolitical regulatory pressure. nl_info.title: AXT Appoints Tracy Liu to Board of Directors
nl_info.sub_title: Board expands to five members as company aligns with AI-driven wafer capacity expansion plans

summary.value: AXT, Inc. announced the appointment of Tracy Liu to its board of directors, effective June 17, which increases the total number of board members from four to five. Liu possesses over 30 years of experience in business consulting, tax strategy, and accounting, including a ten-year tenure at Big Four accounting firms. According to the company's CEO, the appointment is intended to support capacity expansion for Indium Phosphide (InP) wafers driven by artificial intelligence demand.

invest_anal.value: The appointment of Tracy Liu expands AXT's board of directors from four to five members, enhancing the board's professional oversight capabilities. Liu brings over 30 years of experience in business consulting, tax strategy, and accounting, including a decade at Big Four firms. This change in corporate governance structure is specifically aligned with the company's strategic plans for Indium Phosphide (InP) wafer capacity expansion to meet AI-driven demand.

eli_explain.value: AXT, Inc. (AXTI) announced the appointment of Tracy Liu to its Board of Directors, effective June 17, expanding the board from four to five members. Liu brings over 30 years of experience in business consulting, tax strategy, and accounting, including ten years at Big Four firms and a current role as an independent director at ACM Research. Following the announcement, AXT's stock price rose by more than 9%. The appointment aligns with the company's focus on expanding capacity for Indium Phosphide (InP) wafers to meet demand from AI and high-speed data center applications. [citation 1][citation 2]

The event and related disclosures reflect the following factual developments:
- **Quality**: AXT is enhancing its corporate governance by adding a board member with extensive accounting and tax expertise. The company's recent financial data shows a quarterly net income increase of 54.34%, though year-over-year net income and EPS decreased by 82.9% and 78.43%, respectively. [citation 3]
- **Growth**: The company is pivoting its subsidiary, Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology, toward a Hong Kong listing to align with demand for InP substrates in AI data centers. Recent deals, such as the contract with Casela for InP wafer substrates in 2027, indicate a focus on long-term capacity reservation. [citation 5][citation 2]
- **Momentum**: Market reaction to the board appointment saw the stock rise over 9%. However, more recent trading data shows volatility, with the stock closing down 8.54% at $57.21 on July 10, though it remains up significantly over the past year. Analyst sentiment includes Northland reiterating an Outperform rating with a $125 price target as of late June. [citation 5][citation 6]

AXT has expanded its board to five members with the appointment of Tracy Liu to support its AI-driven capacity expansion. This governance change occurs alongside a strategic shift to list its subsidiary in Hong Kong and the securing of long-term supply agreements for Indium Phosphide substrates. While quarterly financial metrics have shown improvement, the company continues to navigate year-over-year declines and the financial implications of its restructured IPO plans. summary.value: On June 11, 2026, AXT Inc. announced that its subsidiary, Beijing Tongmei Crystal Technology, entered into a long-term supply agreement with Casela. According to SEC filings, Casela has committed to purchasing Indium Phosphide (InP) substrates valued at 173 million RMB (approximately $25.4 million) throughout 2027. This agreement follows AXT's established position in the III-V compound semiconductor substrate market, where it holds a significant global market share.

invest_anal.value: The long-term supply agreement between AXT's subsidiary, Beijing Tongmei, and Casela establishes a specific revenue commitment for the 2027 fiscal year. The contract focuses on Indium Phosphide (InP) substrates, which are utilized in high-growth sectors such as AI infrastructure and data centers, representing a documented expansion of the company's future order book.

eli_explain.value: On June 11, 2026, AXT Inc. announced that its subsidiary, Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology Co., Ltd., signed a long-term supply agreement with Casela. Under the terms of the agreement, Casela has committed to purchasing indium phosphide (InP) substrates valued at 173 million RMB (approximately $25.4 million) throughout the year 2027. AXT currently maintains an 85.51% controlling interest in Beijing Tongmei, which specializes in III-V compound semiconductor substrates essential for high-performance applications. [Summary][hight_lights]

A specialized ingredient supplier for high-end restaurants has just secured a major reservation for its premium 'indium phosphide' seasonings, with a customer committing to buy $25.4 million worth of the product throughout 2027. This comes as the supplier is significantly expanding its kitchen capacity, recently raising $632.5 million through a public offering to double its production lines by the end of 2026. While the business is currently managing a net loss of $21.3 million from 2025, it is scaling up to meet the growing appetite of the AI data center market. [Summary][citation 1][citation 2][citation 3]

However, the supplier operates under strict local health and safety regulations that require specific permits for every delivery sent abroad. While it recently secured new permits to resume shipments to additional customers—expected to add several million dollars in unforecasted revenue for Q3 2025—the timing of these regulatory approvals remains a critical factor for fulfilling its large-scale orders. The parent company continues to hold an 85.51% stake in this kitchen while preparing for a potential separate listing on the local exchange to further fund its global expansion. [citation 2][citation 4][citation 5][hight_lights]

Quality: AXT maintains an 85.51% controlling interest in Beijing Tongmei, which serves as a scarce upstream asset in the indium phosphide value chain. The company reported a net loss of $21.3 million in 2025 with relatively thin margins, though it holds a dominant footprint in the production of substrates critical for optical connectivity and AI infrastructure. [citation 1][citation 4][citation 3]

Growth: The company is aggressively expanding its manufacturing capacity, aiming for a 25% increase initially and a goal to double capacity by the end of 2026. Recent capital raises, including a $100 million offering followed by a $632.5 million offering at $64.25 per share, are dedicated to scaling InP output and R&D for next-generation substrates. [citation 1][citation 2][citation 6]

Momentum: Market activity has been characterized by significant volatility; the stock previously experienced a 7.8% decline following the $632.5 million equity raise due to dilution concerns. However, the company recently secured export permits from the PRC Ministry of Commerce, enabling the resumption of InP shipments to certain customers which was expected to generate several million dollars in unforecasted revenue for Q3 2025. [citation 5][citation 3][citation 7]

AXT Inc.'s subsidiary has finalized a $25.4 million supply agreement with Casela for 2027, focusing on high-demand indium phosphide substrates. This follows substantial capital raises of over $700 million intended to double production capacity and underscores the company's efforts to navigate complex PRC export permit requirements while scaling for the AI infrastructure market. nl_info.title: AXT Subsidiary Tongmei Signs 173 Million RMB Indium Phosphide Substrate Supply Agreement with Casela
nl_info.sub_title: The long-term agreement for Indium Phosphide wafer substrates is valued at 173 million RMB with deliveries scheduled for 2027

summary.value: Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology, a subsidiary of AXT, Inc., has signed a long-term supply agreement with Casela for Indium Phosphide (InP) wafer substrates. The contract, which has a total value of 173 million RMB, stipulates monthly deliveries throughout 2027. According to the terms, Casela is required to make a 50% prepayment within 15 working days of signing, with the remaining balance to be settled by December 31, 2026.

invest_anal.value: The long-term supply agreement establishes a committed revenue stream for AXT's subsidiary, Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology, specifically targeting the 2027 fiscal year. The contract terms, including a 50% prepayment and an 80% minimum purchase volume requirement, provide objective data regarding the company's future order backlog and market expansion in the Indium Phosphide (InP) substrate segment.

eli_explain.value: On June 11, 2026, Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology, a subsidiary of AXT, Inc., entered into a long-term supply agreement with Nanjing Casela for indium phosphide (InP) wafer substrates. The agreement is valued at RMB 173 million (approximately US $25.4 million) for deliveries scheduled monthly throughout 2027. Under the terms, Casela must prepay 50% of the total value within 15 business days of signing and settle the remaining 50% by December 31, 2026. Furthermore, the contract includes a take-or-pay provision requiring Casela to purchase at least 80% of the committed volume or face cancellation fees. [citation 1][citation 2][citation 3]

A specialized supplier that provides essential high-grade ingredients to top-tier kitchens has just secured a massive reservation for the entire 2027 season. A major client, Casela, has committed to a contract worth 173 million RMB, promising to pay half the bill upfront within two weeks and the rest before the first dish is even served. To ensure the kitchen's resources aren't wasted, the client is obligated to take at least 80% of their order or pay a significant penalty.

This deal provides the supplier with clear visibility for next year's kitchen operations, especially as they have recently raised significant capital to expand their cooking capacity. While the supplier has faced previous challenges with shifting ingredient export rules and high overhead costs, this guaranteed booking helps fill their upcoming schedule. Meanwhile, some of the restaurant's original owners chose this moment of high activity to reduce their personal stakes in the business. [citation 1][citation 3]

Quality: AXT specializes in compound semiconductor substrates like indium phosphide, which are critical for AI and data center optical connectivity. While the company recorded a net loss of $21.3 million in 2025 and has dealt with thin margins, it maintains a significant market position through its subsidiary Tongmei. [citation 4][citation 5][citation 6]

Growth: The company is aggressively expanding its InP manufacturing capacity by 25%, with plans to double it by the end of 2026 to meet surging AI-driven demand. To fund this, AXT completed two major equity raises: $100 million in late 2025 and approximately $632.5 million in April 2026. [citation 7][citation 8][citation 9]

Momentum: Following the contract announcement and subsequent insider sales of over $1.6 million by directors David C. Chang and Jesse Chen, the stock experienced high volatility, including a double-digit slide followed by a 14% rebound on June 17, 2026. Analyst firm TipRanks currently rates the stock as 'Neutral,' citing constructive near-term profitability guidance but noting ongoing losses and valuation concerns. [citation 3]

AXT's subsidiary Tongmei has secured a RMB 173 million supply contract for 2027, providing significant revenue visibility and advance cash flow through strict prepayment terms. This agreement follows massive capital raises aimed at expanding capacity for AI-related demand, though the company continues to navigate historical losses, insider share sales, and complex international export regulations. nl_info.title: AXT Shares Rise 10% Following Reports of Potential Chinese Export Restrictions on Indium Phosphide
nl_info.sub_title: AXT stock increased 10% as reports indicated potential supply constraints for Indium Phosphide used in optical applications

summary.value: On Friday, AXT, Inc. (AXTI) saw its stock price increase by 10% following reports that China may impose export licensing restrictions on Indium Phosphide (InP). AXT operates as a vertically integrated producer with raw material ownership and manufacturing facilities located in China. Wedbush analysts maintained their 'Outperform' rating and a $93 price target for the company, noting that potential supply limitations and subsequent price increases could impact the company's valuation.

invest_anal.value: The report highlights AXT's vertical integration and ownership of raw materials within China as a factor in its business quality. Potential export licensing restrictions on Indium Phosphide (InP) substrates by China may create supply constraints for the global market, whereas AXT's established manufacturing and supply chain presence within China provides a distinct operational structure. This positioning relates to the company's competitive advantage and supply chain stability under changing regulatory environments. According to Wedbush, these supply dynamics and potential price increases are relevant to the company's fundamental valuation.

eli_explain.value: AXT, Inc. (AXTI) shares rose 10% following reports that China may impose export licensing restrictions on indium phosphide (InP), a critical material for AI optical connectivity. AXT operates a vertically integrated production model with manufacturing facilities in China and has recently navigated similar export permit requirements since early 2025. Wedbush analysts maintained an 'Outperform' rating and a $93 price target, suggesting that potential supply limitations and price increases for InP substrates could influence the company's valuation. [citation 1][citation 2][citation 3]

AXT operates like a specialty restaurant chain that owns its own spice farms in a specific region, providing the essential ingredients for high-end AI 'data dishes' that other kitchens cannot easily replicate. Recently, the local government where those farms are located introduced new red tape for shipping these spices abroad. While this created a backlog of orders and a dip in annual revenue from $99 million to $88.3 million, the restaurant’s profit margins began to recover, jumping from a negative 6.1% to nearly 30% as they secured new permits.

Because these specific spices are becoming twice as necessary for the next generation of menu items, the restaurant is doubling its kitchen capacity through 2026. Even though the shipping rules remain unpredictable, the demand from hungry customers is reaching record levels, and the restaurant is currently projecting its busiest quarter yet as it works through a massive pile of advance orders.

The event highlights several key factual dimensions for AXT:

- **Quality**: AXT is a vertically integrated producer of compound semiconductor substrates, maintaining a significant market share in indium phosphide (InP) wafers. While the company recorded a GAAP net loss of $21.3 million in 2025 due to export delays, its non-GAAP gross margins recently improved to 29.9% from 21.5% in the previous quarter. [citation 1][citation 4]
- **Growth**: The company is expanding its InP manufacturing capacity by 25% with plans to double it by late 2026 or 2027 to meet demand for 1.6T optical modules. Revenue in Q1 2026 reached $26.9 million, a 15% sequential increase, and management expects InP demand to continue doubling annually through 2027. [citation 5][citation 6][citation 4]
- **Momentum**: AXT's stock has exhibited significant volatility, recently rising 10% on the export restriction reports and showing a 276% year-to-date increase as of April 2026. Analysts have raised blended price targets to $96.50, citing stronger AI-related demand across communications and data center hardware. [citation 7][citation 8]
- **Market Sentiment**: Wedbush maintains an 'Outperform' rating with a $93 target, while other analysts note that supply-demand gaps for InP could exceed 70% by 2025, potentially benefiting established suppliers if export permits are managed successfully. [citation 3]

AXT's 10% stock rise reflects market reaction to potential Chinese export restrictions on indium phosphide, a material essential for AI data center infrastructure. While these restrictions introduce regulatory uncertainty and have caused past shipment delays, the company is actively doubling its production capacity to address a growing order backlog and high demand for next-generation optical connectivity.

More critically, the production of indium phosphide substrates is highly dependent on metallic indium, which is a by-product metal primarily recovered from the smelting processes of zinc, tin, and other non-ferrous metals, making it impossible to expand production independently. nl_info.title: AXT Inc. Shares Record 8,335% Annual Increase as Wedbush Raises Price Target
nl_info.sub_title: Wedbush Securities raised its price target for AXT Inc. from $28 to $93, citing a $100 million order backlog

summary.value: AXT Inc. (AXTI), a semiconductor supplier specializing in indium phosphide wafers for AI data centers, has recorded a share price increase of 8,335% over the past year. The company reported an order backlog exceeding $100 million and is currently expanding its production capacity to meet demand. In response to these developments, Wedbush Securities adjusted its price target for the stock to $93, up from a previous target of $28.

invest_anal.value: The company reported a substantial order backlog exceeding $100 million, primarily driven by demand for indium phosphide wafers in AI data centers. This backlog represents a significant increase in future revenue potential. Furthermore, the company is actively expanding its production capacity to meet this heightened demand. Wedbush Securities cited these growth factors as the basis for raising its price target from $28 to $93.

eli_explain.value: AXT Inc. (AXTI) has experienced a significant increase in market activity, characterized by a reported 12-month share price rise of 8,335%. The company recently announced Q2 FY26 revenue of $47.59 million, a 164.8% increase year-over-year, driven by record demand for indium phosphide (InP) substrates used in AI data centers. Gross margins expanded to 44.9% from 8% in the previous year. Furthermore, the company reported an order backlog exceeding $100 million and secured over $65 million in new capacity agreements, including prepayments and deposits from major customers. Wedbush Securities subsequently raised its price target for AXTI to $93 from $28, maintaining an outperform rating. [citation 1][citation 2][citation 3][citation 4]

Imagine a specialized restaurant chain that provides a unique ingredient essential for high-end banquets. For a long time, the restaurant operated with very thin margins, but it has recently seen a dramatic transformation. Revenue has more than doubled as demand for its signature ingredient spiked by 165% year-over-year, and the kitchen's profit margin on each dish jumped from a modest 8% to nearly 45%.

Because of its unique offerings, the restaurant now has a massive waitlist of customers, with a backlog of prepaid reservations and deposits totaling over $65 million. To keep up, the owners have secured hundreds of millions in funding to expand their kitchen capacity. Industry critics have taken notice, significantly raising their expectations for the restaurant's future earnings as it transitions from a period of losses to a record-breaking level of activity driven by a surge in banquet bookings.

Quality: AXT's fundamental profile has shifted from a non-GAAP loss of $0.15 per share a year ago to an adjusted profit of $0.19 per share in Q2 FY26. The company’s gross profit reached $21.37 million, and its interest income turned positive following a secondary offering that raised substantial capital for expansion. [citation 3][citation 4]
Growth: The company is experiencing a trajectory driven by AI infrastructure, with Q2 InP revenue hitting a record high. Management forecasts Q3 non-GAAP diluted earnings per share to reach $0.30 to $0.32, supported by $66 million in revenue that has obtained necessary export permits. [citation 4]
Momentum: Market reaction has been volatile but strong, with the stock surging over 25% in after-hours trading following the Q2 report. AXT currently holds a Zacks Rank #1. However, analysts note that the P/S ratio of 39.4x is significantly higher than the US semiconductor industry average of 7.4x, suggesting the market has priced in high growth expectations. [citation 5][citation 4]

AXT Inc. has reported a 164.8% year-over-year revenue increase and record demand for its indium phosphide substrates, leading to a substantial order backlog and a raised price target of $93 from Wedbush Securities. While the company has reached a turning point in profitability and is expanding capacity to meet AI data center needs, market analysts have highlighted high valuation multiples relative to industry peers. This shift reflects better cost absorption as the company scales its production capacity to meet a backlog that has surpassed $100 million [citation 3].

Even though there is now more total money invested in the business, the restaurant has started selling a new, highly profitable specialty dish (Indium Phosphide for AI transceivers) that is much more efficient to produce. Because the losses are shrinking rapidly while the new kitchen is getting busy, the return on the owner's total investment is now much closer to turning a profit than it was last season.

nl_info.title: AXT Completes $632.5 Million Equity Financing; Shares Fall Over 8%
nl_info.sub_title: AXT raised $632.5 million to expand Indium Phosphide (InP) capacity, resulting in an 8% share price decline

summary.value: Semiconductor substrate manufacturer AXT, Inc. (AXTI.US) announced the completion of an equity financing round totaling $632.5 million. The company stated that the proceeds will be primarily used to expand its Indium Phosphide (InP) production capacity to meet growing demand for AI infrastructure. Following the announcement of the new share issuance, AXT's stock price declined by more than 8% during intraday trading.

invest_anal.value: The financing is specifically earmarked for the expansion of Indium Phosphide (InP) production capacity. This capital expenditure is intended to scale operations to meet the increasing demand for AI infrastructure. The expansion represents a factual increase in the company's potential production output and addressable market size within the semiconductor substrate industry.

The completion of the $632.5 million equity financing involves the issuance of new shares, which increases the total shares outstanding. This typically results in the dilution of existing shareholders' equity and affects per-share valuation metrics. Concurrently, the stock price experienced an intraday decline of over 8% following the announcement, altering the market capitalization and price-to-earnings (P/E) or price-to-book (P/B) ratios based on the new share count and market price.

nl_info.title: AXT Inc. Announces Proposed Public Offering of Common Stock
nl_info.sub_title: Successfully closed equity offering, raising approx. $550 million for Beijing subsidiary's indium phosphide substrate capacity expansion, R&D, and general corporate purposes

summary.value: Semiconductor materials supplier AXT Inc. (AXTI.US) has successfully closed its public equity offering, issuing approximately 8.56 million shares (precisely 8,560,311) at $64.25 per share, raising gross proceeds of about $550 million before underwriting discounts. Net proceeds will primarily support capacity expansion for indium phosphide substrates, R&D projects, and general corporate purposes at its subsidiary, Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology. The underwriter holds a 30-day option to purchase an additional ~1.284 million shares, which could increase total proceeds to approximately $632.5 million. Following the announcement, the stock fell 11.99% in pre-market trading to $69.35. Executives face a 60-day lock-up period, with Northland Capital Markets leading the offering alongside several co-managers.

invest_anal.value: The announcement of a secondary public offering of common stock directly affects the company's valuation framework by increasing the total number of shares outstanding. This issuance results in the dilution of per-share metrics such as Earnings Per Share (EPS) and Book Value Per Share (BVPS). The 6.5% decline in the stock price to $73.61 in after-hours trading represents a factual adjustment to the price component (numerator) of valuation ratios like P/E and P/B. The final impact on valuation multiples will depend on the total number of shares issued and the final offering price relative to the current market price.

eli_explain.value: AXT Inc. announced an underwritten public offering of 8,560,311 shares of common stock at a price of $64.25 per share, resulting in gross proceeds of approximately $550 million. [citation 1][citation 2] Following the announcement, the stock price fell 6.5% to $73.61 in after-hours trading. [Summary] The underwriters subsequently exercised their over-allotment option in full to purchase an additional 1,284,046 shares, bringing the total gross proceeds to approximately $632.5 million. [citation 3][citation 2] The company intends to use the net proceeds to support capacity expansion at its Beijing subsidiary, fund research and development, and for general corporate purposes. [Summary][citation 4]

AXT Inc., a specialist in high-performance semiconductor substrates like indium phosphide and gallium arsenide, recently completed a substantial capital raise through a public offering of over 9.8 million shares at $64.25 per share. The company reported a second-quarter profit and successfully increased its cash reserves, supported by these gross proceeds of $632.5 million. This financial activity follows a previous smaller offering in December 2025 where shares were priced at $12.25. Additionally, the company has secured a long-term supply agreement with Lumentum for wafer capacity, signaling steady demand for its specialized materials in sectors like 5G and data centers.

Imagine a specialized restaurant chain that produces unique ingredients other kitchens cannot replicate. To keep up with growing demand for these ingredients, the chain decides to issue a large number of new membership shares to the public to fund the building of larger production facilities and the development of new recipes. While the sudden increase in available memberships caused the market value of existing shares to dip by 6.5%, the restaurant successfully filled its coffers with $632.5 million in new capital. With a major client already signing a long-term contract to reserve future table space and ingredients, the restaurant is focused on expanding its operations to meet the technical needs of its sophisticated clientele.

Quality: AXT reported a strong profit and cash build in Q2 2026, maintaining a manufacturing presence in three Chinese locations and partial ownership in ten raw material suppliers to manage its supply chain. [citation 3][citation 5] Growth: The company entered a long-term supplier agreement with Lumentum for indium phosphide substrates to support demand in 5G infrastructure and data centers. [citation 5] Momentum: Market data shows AXTI shares dropped 12% following the $550 million discounted offering, though the stock has historically shown high volatility with a two-year annualized return of 452.96% and a recent 2.8% weekly rise to $2.20 before the major offering events. [citation 6][citation 7][citation 8]

AXT Inc. has finalized a public offering totaling 9,844,357 shares, including the full exercise of the over-allotment option, raising approximately $632.5 million in gross proceeds. [citation 3][citation 2] The capital is earmarked for expansion in Beijing and research initiatives, while the company concurrently secured a long-term capacity reservation agreement with Lumentum. [Summary][citation 5]

# AXT, Inc. Announces Proposed Public Offering of Common Stock. (NASDAQ:AXTI), a leading manufacturer of compound semiconductor substrates, today announced that it intends to offer and sell shares of its common stock in an underwritten public offering. AXT intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes, which may include the relocation of its gallium arsenide product line, working capital, capital expenditures and other corporate expenses. A shelf registration statement relating to the shares of common stock was previously filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) and declared effective on November 4, 2016. A preliminary prospectus supplement and accompanying prospectus relating to the offering will be filed with the SEC and will be available on the SEC’s website. nl_info.sub_title: Annual revenue decreased 11.1% to $88.3 million with a net loss of $23.2 million

summary.value: AXT, Inc. reported its financial results for the full year of 2025, recording total revenue of $88.3 million, an 11.1% decrease compared to the previous year. The company saw a net loss of $23.2 million, representing a loss of $0.49 per share. Management attributed the decline to reduced substrate sales, rising fixed costs, and export license restrictions that led to a significant revenue drop in the North American market, though China remained its largest market.

invest_anal.value: The company's financial report indicates a contraction in business scale for the fiscal year 2025. Total revenue declined by 11.1% year-over-year, driven by reduced substrate sales and regulatory impacts such as export license restrictions in North America. The bottom-line growth was negative, resulting in a net loss of $23.2 million compared to the previous period. Furthermore, the company significantly reduced its investment in long-term growth drivers, with research and development expenditures decreasing by 37.8% year-over-year.

eli_explain.value: AXT, Inc. released its fiscal year 2025 results, reporting total revenue of $88.3 million, an 11.1% decrease from $99.4 million in 2024. [citation 1] The company recorded a GAAP net loss of $21.3 million, or $0.49 per share, compared to a net loss of $11.6 million in the previous year. [citation 1] GAAP gross margin compressed to 12.7% from 24.0% in 2024. [citation 1] Operating expenses for the year were $33.2 million, a decrease from $38.6 million in 2024, while research and development expenditures fell by 37.8% year-over-year. [citation 1]

In 2025, the restaurant chain faced a challenging environment, with annual sales dropping from $99.4 million to $88.3 million. Despite serving fewer customers, the costs of keeping the kitchens running remained high, causing the profit margin on each meal to drop from 24.0% to 12.7%. Consequently, the chain's total annual loss widened from $11.6 million to $21.3 million, and the loss per share reached $0.49. To manage these pressures, the company reduced its spending on developing new menu items by 37.8%.

However, by the second quarter of 2026, the restaurant saw a sharp reversal in performance. Revenue surged 164% year-over-year to $47.6 million, and the chain returned to profitability with earnings of $0.19 per share. The margin on meals improved significantly to 45.0% during this period, driven by high demand for specialty ingredients used in advanced technology infrastructure. The company also secured long-term supply agreements, signaling a shift in its business momentum compared to the previous fiscal year.

Quality: AXT's fundamental metrics for fiscal 2025 showed a decline in profitability, with GAAP gross margins falling to 12.7% and a widened annual net loss of $21.3 million. [citation 1] However, by Q2 2026, the company reported a non-GAAP gross margin expansion to 45.0% and a return to profitability. [citation 2] Growth: While 2025 revenue declined 11.1% to $88.3 million, AXT reported record quarterly revenue of $47.6 million in Q2 2026, a 164% year-over-year increase. [citation 2][citation 1] Analysts expect earnings to grow by 231.58% in the coming year, reaching $0.63 per share. [citation 3] Momentum: The stock price has risen 65% over a two-week period as of August 13, 2026, following the Q2 2026 earnings beat. [citation 4] Market sentiment is reflected in analyst revisions, with Zacks reporting that covering analysts have raised earnings estimates for the next quarter and full year. [citation 5]

AXT, Inc. concluded fiscal year 2025 with an 11.1% revenue decline to $88.3 million and a net loss of $21.3 million, impacted by reduced substrate sales and margin compression. [citation 1] Despite these annual figures, the company's subsequent Q2 2026 results showed record revenue of $47.6 million and a return to profitability, driven by demand for data center optical connectivity and new supply agreements. [citation 2][citation 6]

invest_anal.value: The company reported a contraction in full-year revenue and a shift from profitability to a net loss for the fiscal year 2025. Quarterly results were impacted by specific external constraints regarding export licenses. Management has indicated that future expansion is expected to be driven by Indium Phosphide (InP) sales for data centers, supported by long-term supply agreements extending through 2028.

eli_explain.value: AXT, Inc. reported its fourth quarter and full year 2025 financial results, showing a total annual revenue of $88.3 million, an 11% decrease from $99.4 million in 2024. [citation 1][citation 2][citation 3] The company recorded a full-year non-GAAP net loss of $18.0 million ($0.41 per share), compared to a net income of $8.5 million ($0.20 per share) in 2024. [citation 2] Despite these challenges, AXT's cash and cash equivalents increased to $120.3 million by year-end 2025, aided by a $93.9 million public offering closed in December. [citation 1][citation 2]

A specialty restaurant chain experienced a slowdown in 2025, with its total annual sales dropping by 11% and its previous profit turning into a net loss of $18 million. During the final quarter of the year, the kitchen faced significant delays in receiving essential imported ingredients, which prevented it from fulfilling a portion of its customer orders and resulted in quarterly revenue falling short of the manager's expectations. While the restaurant's overall profit margins for the year were lower than the previous year, they showed a slight improvement in the final months compared to the same period a year ago.

Despite these temporary ingredient shortages, the restaurant has secured long-term contracts to supply high-demand dishes through 2028 and recently received a massive cash injection from new investors, bringing its reserves to over $120 million. The manager is now preparing to double the capacity of its most popular kitchen line by the end of 2026 to meet a record-high backlog of orders from major corporate clients. For the start of 2026, the restaurant expects to serve more customers as it has already secured the necessary permits for a significant portion of its upcoming menu.

Quality: AXT's fundamental profile in 2025 was characterized by a shift from profitability to a GAAP net loss of $21.3 million and a decrease in GAAP gross margin to 12.7% from 24.0% in 2024. [citation 1] However, the balance sheet strengthened significantly, with total stockholders' equity rising to $296.6 million and cash reserves exceeding $120 million following a capital raise. [citation 1][citation 2]

Growth: The company is positioned in a growth cycle tied to AI infrastructure and data center connectivity, with an indium phosphide (InP) backlog reaching a record $60 million by the end of Q4 2025. [citation 2][citation 4] Management plans to double InP manufacturing capacity by the end of 2026 and has signed long-term supply agreements with Coherent and Lumentum extending through 2028 and beyond. [citation 2][citation 3]

Momentum: Market data indicates significant volatility; the stock price and trading volume increased in late 2025 and early 2026, though a 17% one-day decline was noted in March 2026 without a specific catalyst. [citation 5][citation 6] B. Riley Securities maintained a Neutral rating on July 31, 2026, while raising the price target from $52 to $55. This includes fourth-quarter 2025 revenue of $23m, down  8.4% on $25.1m a year ago and 17.8% on $28m in Q3/2025 (although the latter had far exceeded the guidance for  Q3 of $19–21m, spiking from just $18m in Q2). Q4 revenue was below the initial guidance of $27–30m,  due mainly to fewer-than-expected export control  permits for indium phosphide being  issued by China’s Ministry of Commerce. The China government imposed  trade restrictions on export of GaAs in August 2023 and InP in February 2025,  aiming to restrict the export of materials used for military applications and  requiring an export permit for every customer order. AXT was granted its first  permit for exporting InP in late June 2025. Of total  revenue in Q4, the proportion from the Asia Pacific region was 81.5% (down  from 87% in Q3), whereas Europe was 17.5% (up from 12% in Q3), and North  America remained just 1% (compared with 10% a year ago). The proportion of  revenue coming from the top five customers fell back, from 45.2% last quarter  (with two customers exceeding 10%) to just 22.6% in Q4/2025 (with no customers  exceeding 10%).  Indium phosphide revenue was $8m (down  from $9.1m a year ago and Q3/2025’s three-year high of $13.1m, but still more  than double Q2’s $3.6m), primarily from data-center applications. Gallium arsenide revenue was $7m, down  from $7.5m last quarter but up on $5.4m a year ago. Also, AXT saw an uptick in  semiconducting wafers for both industrial laser and data-center laser  applications.   Germanium substrate revenue was $0.23m, down from $0.64m in Q3 and  $1.6m a year ago. Compared with  $9m a year ago, revenue has recovered somewhat from Q3/2025’s $6.7m to Q4’s  $7.6m for the two consolidated raw material joint venture companies:  BoYu (which makes high-temperature pyrolytic boron nitride crucibles and  pBN-based tools for organic light-emitting diodes) and JinMei (which supplies  high-purity materials including gallium and germanium, as well as InP poly and  other materials).   On a non-GAAP basis, full-year gross margin has fallen from 24.3% in  2024 to 13.1% for 2025. However, although quarterly gross margin fell back down  slightly from 22.6% in Q3 to 21.5% in Q4, this was up on 17.9% a year ago.   Quarterly operating expenses were $7.15m in Q4, up on a lower-than-normal  $6.66m in Q3 (which had some favorable adjustments  in R&D) but cut from $9.9m a year ago. Full-year OpEx has been cut from $35.9m  in 2024 to $30.2m for 2025.   Compared with net income of $8.5m ($0.20 per share) for full-year 2024,  full-year 2025 returned a net loss of $18m ($0.41 per share). Quarterly net loss rose from $1.17m ($0.03 per share) in Q3 to $2.27m ($0.05 per share, more than the  initial guidance of $0.01–0.03) in Q4. However, this is a cut from $4.34m ($0.10 per share) a year ago.   After falling by a further 3.9m in Q3/2025, during  Q4/2025 cash, cash equivalents and investments was boosted by $97.2m, from  $31.2m to $128.4m. This was due mainly to $93.9m raised from the public  offering of common stock that closed on 30 December. Net inventory rose back up by $4m, from $77.7m to $81.7m, although this  is still below the $85.1m a year ago. “This continues to be a focus for  us, and we expect to bring it down in coming quarters,” says chief  financial officer Gary Fischer. Return to revenue growth  and reduced losses expected in Q1/2026  “We were disappointed that we didn’t receive as many export permits  in Q4 as we had hoped based on the average processing time we had seen up  to that point in October. The good news is now that we have received permits in  Q1,” says CEO Morris Young. “We have approximately $26m in revenue  that can be realized in Q1 across our substrate product lines and raw  materials, for which we either already have a permit to ship or for which an  export permit is not required,” says Fischer. “We could see significant upside  to this number in Q1 should we receive more permits for additional orders  between now and the end of the quarter,” he adds. With OpEx expected to remain  about $9m in Q1, net loss should be cut to $0.02–0.04 per share.  “This represents substantial year-over-year progress towards our return to  profitability,” notes Fischer.   “We expect to achieve sequential growth in revenue in Q1, driven  primarily by growth in indium phosphide for data-center build-out for AI,” says Young. “As we  enter 2026 as a foundational supplier to this multi-year growth cycle, we are  notably broadening our customer base to include tier-1 companies [in the  optical space] to which we have previously had limited exposure. This  includes tier-1 laser manufacturers and optical transceiver module makers both  in China and around the world,” he adds. “Our backlog for indium phosphide wafers  has reached a new high of over $60m [up from Q3’s record of $49m, which had more  than doubled from Q2]. Customers are planning for longer lead-time by placing  longer-term orders and giving us more visibility into their expected demand,”  notes Young. “The supply chain for optical transceiver is quite complex  and highly globalized. We believe this geographical interdependence is  providing both opportunity and incentives for the ecosystem to work together in  new ways to solve global supply chain shortages.” “Beyond pluggable receivers, we are seeing  a very large developing market for co-packaged optics for both scale-up and  scale-out applications. We’re actively engaging in discussions with our  customers about their technical and timing requirements and believe this could  represent yet another inflection point in our business, developing in late  2027 and beyond,” Young says. “From a geographic demand perspective, the  massive AI infrastructure build-out and planned CapEx spending by cloud  services and AI platform providers in the USA is the primary driver for  EML [electro-absorption modulated lasers]  and silicon photonic-based optical transceivers… Our materials are being  used in multiple US hyperscalers and we expect that end-customers’ use  will continue to broaden. In China, the data-center build-out is early in its  ramp. But we are seeing rapid growth as China moves to accelerate its  data-center expansion and AI capabilities. Our revenue related to the  data-center market in China are expected to grow by more than 60% in Q1 over  Q4, highlighting both increased investment in these tier-1 data centers as  well as the strong desire for Chinese domestic suppliers to secure local stores  at every level of the AI infrastructure supply chain.” InP  production capacity to double in 2026, and possibly double again in 2027 “Given the strong demand environment, it  is important to note that AXT is well positioned to handle increased demand for  indium phosphide wafers,” says Young. Since October, AXT has added about  25% more capacity, and is on track with its current plan to double capacity  from Q4/2025 by the end of 2026, supporting a $35m quarterly InP revenue  run-rate. This should require no more than $30m in CapEx due to using mainly  brownfield space in the existing Tongmei facility (where  there is already an existing building with a cleanroom available, with a  power supply, water etc). “Beyond  our current plan for capacity expansion, we’re working closely with our  customer base to understand their long-term requirements and to align our  plans globally,” says Young. Beyond 2026, AXT is looking at possibly doubling  capacity again in 2027, costing $100–150m in CapEx, due to needing greenfield  construction, he adds. “Our recent capital raise will be  fundamental to our future expansion as we enter our next significant phase of  growth. A major focus of this expansion will be an increased investment in our  6-inch indium phosphide product, and we are excited to work with our  customers to meet the rigorous requirements of next-generation EML and silicon  photonic-based devices,” Young says. “We’re a fundamental supplier to the  multi-year optical build-out in the AI infrastructure market, we have a  broadening customer base of tier-1 companies, and a strong balance sheet to  support our continued business expansion,” he summarizes. “In gallium arsenide, we continue to see  demand for semi-insulating wafers for wireless RF devices and believe that we  have strong opportunity for market share expansion, gated primarily by our  ability to obtain export permits,” says Young. “In Q4, we saw an uptake in  semiconducting wafers for both industrial laser applications and  data-center laser applications. VCSELs [vertical-cavity surface-emitting  lasers] for data-center applications typically do not require a lot of  gallium arsenide material as the devices are small, so they don’t move the  needle much as a growth driver for us. However, we are seeing increased demand  for VCSEL for autonomous vehicles in China in the Chinese automobile  market, which is currently expanding rapidly.” Young also highlights emerging  application in robotics, where VCSELs can increase the precision and dexterity  of a modern robotic hand. “Compared to the VCSELs used in data-center  applications, machine-vision VCSELs tend to be very large and use more GaAs  substrates. They also require high-quality material, which we are very well  positioned to supply,” he notes. “Again, demand is more today, primarily  China-based, and covers a diverse set of customers, but the breadth of use-case  and the development is very exciting.” STAR Market listing update On 10 January  2022, AXT’s China-based wafer manufacturing subsidiary Beijing Tongmei Xtal  Technology Co Ltd submitted its application to list its shares in an initial  public offering on the Shanghai Stock Exchange’s Sci-Tech innovAtion boaRd  (STAR Market) and the application was accepted for review.Subsequently,  Tongmei responded to several rounds of questions received from the Shanghai  Stock Exchange (SSE). On 12 July 2022, the SSE approved the listing  of Tongmei’s shares. On 1 August 2022, the China Securities Regulatory  Commission (CSRC) accepted Tongmei’s IPO application for review. The STAR Market  IPO remains subject to review and approval by the CSRC and other authorities. nl_info.sub_title: Company expects scale-out orders to double in 2026 and again in 2027 driven by AI data center demand

summary.value: AXT, Inc., a leading supplier of Indium Phosphide (InP) substrates, announced that its co-packaged optics (CPO) business is expected to enter a period of significant growth between 2028 and 2029. This projection aligns with broader industry shifts toward 1.6T networking and next-generation AI chip architectures. Management noted that demand for InP remains robust despite geopolitical pressures related to export controls, as the material is critical for high-power laser chips used in AI data centers.

invest_anal.value: AXT has issued forward-looking guidance projecting a significant expansion in its Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) business. The company forecasts a specific growth trajectory for scale-out orders, anticipating they will double in 2026 and double again in 2027. This growth is linked to the deployment of 1.6T networking and AI data center demand for Indium Phosphide (InP) substrates. The 2028-2029 period is identified by management as the primary window for large-scale commercial deployment of CPO and Near-Package Optics (NPO) technologies.

eli_explain.value: AXT, Inc. announced a significant growth outlook for its co-packaged optics (CPO) business, projecting a major deployment window between 2028 and 2029. The company expects scale-out orders to double in 2026 and double again in 2027, driven by AI data center demand for Indium Phosphide (InP) substrates. To address supply shortages for high-power laser chips, AXT has secured a supply agreement with Lumentum. This expansion coincides with Lumentum's reported surge in demand and its need for additional substrate support to meet the 1.6T networking and next-generation AI architecture requirements.

AXT operates like a specialized supplier of high-grade organic ingredients to a major restaurant chain. Currently, the chain is seeing record-breaking demand, with its total annual revenue jumping from $1.65 billion to $3.01 billion, and its component sales growing by nearly 80%. Because the restaurant is shifting to a new, high-efficiency kitchen setup called 'CPO' to serve faster meals, it has turned to AXT to secure a steady supply of these essential ingredients, ensuring it can keep up with a doubling of orders expected over the next two years.

While the restaurant is currently profitable with gross margins exceeding 50% and earnings per share reaching $3.23 in the latest quarter, it is preparing for a massive grand opening of its most advanced dining concept in 2028. AXT's role is to provide the raw materials today so the restaurant can handle the influx of customers expected when these new high-speed service technologies become the industry standard toward the end of the decade.

Quality: AXT’s fundamentals are tied to the rising demand for Indium Phosphide, a critical material for high-power lasers. Its partner, Lumentum, reported a fiscal year 2026 revenue of $3.01 billion, up 83.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margins surpassing 50% and non-GAAP EPS of $3.23. [citation 1][citation 2]

Growth: The company anticipates a doubling of scale-out orders in both 2026 and 2027. Industry forecasts suggest the CPO market could exceed $20 billion by 2036 with a 37% CAGR. Lumentum expects high-volume laser shipments for optical Scale Up to begin in the second half of 2027 to support 2028 deployments. [citation 3][citation 4]

Momentum: Market sentiment is centered on the transition from pluggable modules to CPO/NPO architectures. While some analysts, such as those at SemiAnalysis, previously suggested delays for CPO until 2029, Lumentum and Coherent have clarified that demand signals have increased and production plans for lead customers remain on track for 2027-2028. [citation 5][citation 3][citation 6]

AXT is positioning itself as a key supplier for the 2028-2029 CPO deployment cycle by securing a partnership with Lumentum and forecasting a doubling of orders over the next two years. The outlook is supported by Lumentum's strong fiscal 2026 performance and the broader industry shift toward 1.6T networking and AI-driven optical scale-up.

nl_info.title: AXT Forecasts Indium Phosphide Substrate Orders to Double in 2026 and 2027
nl_info.sub_title: Orders for rack-to-rack connections are expected to double in 2026 and 2027 due to data center transitions to optical signaling

summary.value: At the Needham Growth Conference, AXT, Inc. stated that its Indium Phosphide (InP) substrate orders for rack-to-rack connections are projected to double in 2026 and again in 2027. This growth is driven by the shift in data center infrastructure from copper wiring to optical signals. Following this announcement, several optical communication stocks, including LandMark Optoelectronics and VPEC, reached their daily price limits in regional markets.

invest_anal.value: AXT, Inc. has issued a forward-looking statement regarding the demand for its Indium Phosphide (InP) substrates, forecasting that orders for rack-to-rack connections will double in both 2026 and 2027. This projection is based on the structural transition within data center infrastructure from copper wiring to optical signaling. Furthermore, the company has secured a three-year supply agreement with Lumentum to address anticipated supply requirements during this period.

eli_explain.value: AXT, Inc. (AXTI) reported record second-quarter 2026 results, with revenue surging 164.8% year-over-year to $47.59 million, significantly exceeding the street estimate of $34.09 million. [citation 1] The company's Indium Phosphide (InP) revenue reached a record $30.7 million, driven by demand for AI data center optical connectivity. [citation 1] Adjusted EPS for the quarter was $0.19, beating the consensus estimate of $0.07. [citation 1] Following these results and the company's projection at the Needham Growth Conference that InP substrate orders for rack-to-rack connections would double in 2026 and again in 2027, the stock surged over 36% in premarket trading. [citation 1] Additionally, AXT signed a long-term supply agreement with Lumentum involving $87 million in deposits to secure InP wafer supply through 2031. [citation 2][citation 3]

A specialized ingredient supplier for high-end restaurants has reached a major turning point as the industry shifts toward a new style of gourmet cooking. The company reported that its quarterly sales for its star product, a rare seasoning required for high-speed kitchen operations, reached an all-time high of $30.7 million. This surge helped total quarterly revenue grow by over 160% compared to last year, while profit margins improved significantly from 8.2% to 45.0% due to higher volumes and a more profitable product mix. 

Looking ahead, the supplier plans to double its production capacity by next year and double it again the year after to meet a massive backlog of orders that already exceeds $100 million. Major restaurant chains are so concerned about potential shortages that they have started paying tens of millions of dollars in advance just to reserve their spot in line. The company's kitchen is currently operating at full speed, with management noting that they can sell every unit they are capable of producing as the market moves away from traditional ingredients toward this specialized high-performance alternative.

Quality: AXT demonstrated a significant recovery in fundamentals, with adjusted gross margins expanding to 45.0% from 8.2% a year prior. [citation 1] The company holds a dominant market position, controlling an estimated 60% to 70% of global indium phosphide substrate supply. [citation 4]

Growth: The company is entering a multi-year expansion phase, aiming to double InP capacity in 2026 and again in 2027. [citation 1][citation 5] Management projects Q3 2026 revenue of $66 million, representing approximately 40% sequential growth. [citation 6] This is supported by an InP backlog exceeding $100 million and prepayments totaling $134.7 million from key partners like Lumentum and Coherent. [citation 3][citation 1]

Momentum: The stock has shown significant price action, surging over 36% premarket following the Q2 report and recording a 351% year-to-date increase as of late July 2026. [citation 7][citation 1] Industry analysts, such as those from Shenwan Hongyuan, note that the transition from 800G to 1.6T optical modules doubles the InP requirement per module, contributing to a projected global supply gap of over 70%. [citation 8]

AXT has reported record financial performance driven by a surge in demand for Indium Phosphide substrates used in AI data centers. The company has secured significant long-term supply agreements and prepayments from major industry players and plans to quadruple its production capacity by the end of 2027 to address a persistent global supply-demand gap.

[{"type": "NewsArticle", "id": "294518488", "content": {"author": "", "body": "AXT Inc. (NASDAQ:AXTI) shares are surging premarket on Friday after the company posted strong second-quarter results after Thursday’s closing bell.



Semiconductor wafer manufacturer AXT reported adjusted EPS of 19 cents, which beat the analyst consensus estimate of seven cents, according to Benzinga Pro data.



Revenue rose 164.80% year over year (Y/Y) to $47.59 million, blowing past the Street estimate of $34.09 million.



Adjusted gross margin expanded to 45.0% in the second quarter from 8.2% in the second quarter of 2025, led by higher volumes and favorable product mix.



Adjusted operating profit stood at $11.2 million, better than the loss of $6.1 million in the prior-year quarter.



Cash, cash equivalents, and investments stood at $748.8 million as of June 30, 2026.



Record Indium Phosphide Revenue



Indium phosphide (InP) revenue hit a record $30.7 million, driven by strong demand from AI data center applications.



Morris Young, CEO of AXT, said the company has reached a key inflection point, with strong demand for data center optical connectivity, expanding manufacturing capacity, and improved productivity driving a significant increase in revenue. He highlighted that the second quarter marked AXT’s highest quarterly indium phosphide revenue to date.



Revenue by product category included $6.6 million from gallium arsenide, $272,000 from germanium substrates, and record consolidated raw material joint venture revenue of $10 million. The company’s top five customers accounted for approximately 30% of revenue, with no single customer contributing more than 10%.



InP backlog exceeded $100 million, with demand continuing to outpace supply. Growth is being fueled by AI data center expansion, including adoption of 800G and 1.6 terabit optical transceiver modules, as well as future near-packaged optics and co-packaged optics technologies.



In China, revenue from InP-based laser markets more than doubled sequentially in the second quarter, with further growth expected in the third quarter of 2026.



Outlook & Management Commentary



The company projects third quarter adjusted EPS of 30-32 cents per share (vs consensus of 11 cents) and sales of $66.000 million vs street view of $38.801 million.



It anticipates GAAP EPS of 29 to 31 cents versus the 9 cents estimate.



AXT is on track to double InP production capacity in 2026, driven by faster capacity expansion, improved manufacturing productivity from new crystal growth furnace designs, and customer migration toward larger-diameter substrates and higher-value products.



The company expects to more than triple its InP revenue opportunity by the end of 2026, with further expansion anticipated in 2027. AXT expects AI infrastructure growth to support a multi-year demand cycle for InP materials.



AXTI Price Action: AXT shares were up 36.34% at $64.00 during premarket trading on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

nl_info.title: AXT to Release Q4 2025 Financial Results on February 19, 2026
nl_info.sub_title: Q4 revenue guidance updated to $22.5 million–$23.5 million due to export license counts

summary.value: AXT Inc. has announced it will report its fourth quarter 2025 financial results on February 19, 2026. The company updated its revenue guidance for the quarter to a range of $22.5 million to $23.5 million, citing fewer-than-expected indium phosphide export licenses issued by China's Ministry of Commerce. Despite these challenges, the company stated that product demand remains strong and it intends to proceed with doubling its indium phosphide capacity in the second half of 2025.

invest_anal.value: AXT Inc. has adjusted its Q4 2025 revenue guidance due to external regulatory factors involving export licenses from China's Ministry of Commerce. While the short-term revenue outlook is impacted by these logistical constraints, the company has confirmed plans to proceed with a significant expansion of its indium phosphide production capacity in the second half of 2025, supported by a financing round completed in December. The guidance reflects current export volumes rather than a decline in end-market demand, which the company describes as remaining strong.

eli_explain.value: AXT Inc. reported its fourth quarter 2025 financial results on February 19, 2026. Revenue for the quarter was $23 million, a decrease from $25.1 million in the same period last year, falling within the company's updated guidance range of $22.5 million to $23.5 million. [citation 1][citation 2] The adjusted non-GAAP loss per share was $0.05, an improvement compared to the $0.10 loss per share in Q4 2024. [citation 1] Despite missing the initial revenue estimate of $24.24 million, the company reported a record backlog for indium phosphide (InP) substrates exceeding $60 million, driven by demand for AI infrastructure. [citation 1][citation 2]

A specialized restaurant chain faced a temporary shortage of serving permits from local authorities, leading to quarterly revenue of $23 million compared to $25.1 million the previous year. Despite serving fewer tables than expected, the restaurant managed its kitchen more efficiently, narrowing its loss per share from $0.10 to $0.05. 

While the current dining room was restricted, the restaurant's waiting list for its signature dish surged to a record value of over $60 million. To meet this massive backlog of hungry customers, the owners are moving forward with plans to double their kitchen capacity by the end of 2026. The management noted that the demand for their specialized ingredients is now backed by long-term reservations extending several years into the future.

Quality: AXT reported a negative net margin of 24.07% and a negative return on equity of 10.59% for the quarter. [citation 2] The company maintains a robust balance sheet to support expansion, though it continues to operate at a non-GAAP loss. [citation 1]

Growth: While year-over-year revenue declined due to export license delays, management identified a multi-year growth cycle driven by AI infrastructure. [citation 1] The company plans to double its indium phosphide production capacity by the end of 2026 with a $30 million capital expenditure. [citation 1] Customer demand is reportedly extending as far as 2030, with some providing minimum demand guarantees for the next two to three years. [citation 1]

Momentum: Following the earnings announcement, AXT's stock price surged 24.65% to $29.68 on February 20, 2026. [citation 1] Market reaction was characterized by a 81.53% year-to-date increase as of late February. [citation 1] Analysts have provided a consensus price target of $22.80, with individual targets ranging from B. Riley's $21.00 to UBS Group's $35.00. [citation 2]

AXT Inc. finished Q4 2025 with $23 million in revenue and a $0.05 non-GAAP loss per share. While export license constraints impacted immediate revenue, the company reported a record backlog exceeding $60 million and announced plans to double production capacity to meet long-term demand from the AI infrastructure sector.

nl_info.sub_title: Company issued over 7 million shares at $12.25 per share to fund growth initiatives

summary.value: AXT, Inc. has finalized a follow-on equity financing round, raising approximately $87 million through the issuance of more than 7 million shares of common stock. The offering was priced at $12.25 per share, with the proceeds intended to strengthen the company's capital base and provide financial flexibility for manufacturing improvements and strategic growth plans. Following the announcement, AXT's share price recorded a 27.7% increase.

invest_anal.value: AXT, Inc. has secured approximately $87 million in gross proceeds through a follow-on equity offering. The company has explicitly stated that these funds are intended to finance manufacturing improvements and strategic growth initiatives. This capital injection provides the financial resources necessary for potential expansion of production capacity and the execution of long-term business development plans. The stock price rose by 27.7% following the announcement, reflecting the market's immediate response to the finalized financing.

eli_explain.value: AXT, Inc. (AXTI) has successfully finalized a follow-on equity financing round, raising approximately $87 million in gross proceeds. By issuing 7 million new shares at $12.25 each, the company has successfully secured $87 million in fresh funding to expand its kitchens and upgrade its cooking equipment.

This influx of capital is intended to modernize manufacturing processes and support the company's growth plans. While the issuance of new shares increases the total number of 'membership stakes' in the business, the market responded to the finalized funding and strategic focus on infrastructure with a 27.7% rise in the share price.

The event relates to the following factors: 
- **Quality**: The company is identified as a major wafer supplier within the photonics supply chain. The $87 million in proceeds is intended to strengthen its capital base and support manufacturing improvements to maintain its position in AI chip architecture and optical networking sectors. [citation 1][citation 2]
- **Growth**: AXT is targeting growth initiatives in the semiconductor and optical networking markets, which include AI-driven infrastructure. The company issued these shares specifically to provide the financial flexibility needed to execute these strategic plans.
- **Momentum**: Following the announcement of the financing completion, AXT's stock price rose by 27.7%. External market commentators, such as Xavier Wagner, have attributed a 'Must Buy' rating to the stock following recent cycles, and it has been highlighted as one of several semiconductor stocks added to expanded AI offerings by firms like STARTRADER.
